subject: Logic
title: What Is a Formal System?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is a Formal System?.

hook.text: Chess has pieces, a board, and rules. A formal system has symbols, axioms, and inference rules.

buildup.text: A formal system defines a language (symbols), starting truths (axioms), and rules for deriving new truths.

discovery.text: Euclidean geometry is one: five axioms, clear rules, and every theorem ever proven follows from them.

twist.text: Change one axiom (like the parallel postulate) and you get a completely different geometry.

climax.text: Formal systems are truth machines—but they're only as good as their axioms and rules.

punchline.text: Axioms define the universe of truths.

quiz.question: What are the components of a formal system?
